faq.q: How do I book a ticket?
faq.a: Search for your route, choose a trip, pick your seats, enter passenger names and pay. The ticket with a QR code arrives by email and stays in My trips.

faq.q: How long are my seats held?
faq.a: 30 minutes. If the payment is not completed in time, the seats are released automatically.
Yes, until 2 hours before departure. Paid tickets are refunded to the original payment method.
One piece of hand luggage per passenger is free. A large suitcase costs a small fixed fee that is shown before you pay.

faq.q: What if my trip is cancelled?
faq.a: You are notified by email, the booking is cancelled and you are refunded in full.

footer.demo: Demo project: payments run in test mode, no real tickets are sold.
footer.built: Built with Next.js, NestJS and PostgreSQL

sections.p: BusTravel is a portfolio project. It is not a real transport company and sells no real tickets.

When you sign up we store your name, email address and a hashed password. When you book we store the trip, the seats and the passenger names you enter. We never see or store card details: payments run in test mode.

We only use strictly necessary cookies: two sign-in cookies that keep you logged in (scripts cannot read them) and your language choice. There are no advertising or tracking cookies, so there is no cookie banner. Your choice of departure city on the home page stays in your browser only.
The location button on the home page asks your browser for permission. Your position is used once, inside your browser, to find the nearest city. It is never sent to our servers.
Data is kept only to run the demo and may be erased at any time.
BusTravel shows how an online bus booking service could work. Routes, prices and timetables are examples and do not describe real journeys.
A selected seat is held for 30 minutes. Payment runs in test mode: no money is taken and no real tickets are issued.
Keep your password safe. You are responsible for what happens under your account.
City photos come from Wikimedia Commons. Authors and licences are listed under Photo credits in the footer.
The service is provided as it is, without any guarantee that it is always available or error free.
BusTravel is a non-commercial portfolio project run by its author.
It demonstrates a full web stack: Next.js front end, NestJS API, PostgreSQL database and automated deployment.
